Which of these animals eliminates 1 gm of its nitrogenous waste with the smallest quantity of water?

distractor_rationale.B: The shark is ureotelic, so about 50 ml of water per gram is needed; it is economical compared with an ammonotelic animal but not the most economical here.

options.C: P spends less energy in producing its waste but needs more water to eliminate it than Q

options.B: Minor calyx --> renal papilla --> major calyx --> renal pelvis --> ureter
options.C: Renal papilla --> minor calyx --> major calyx --> renal pelvis --> ureter
options.D: Renal papilla --> minor calyx --> renal pelvis --> major calyx --> ureter

correct_answer_text: Renal papilla --> minor calyx --> major calyx --> renal pelvis --> ureter

distractor_rationale.A: The two calyces are interchanged; several minor calyces open into a major calyx, so the minor one is met first.
distractor_rationale.B: This places the calyx before the papilla, whereas the papilla is the tip of the pyramid from which urine leaves the kidney substance.
distractor_rationale.D: The renal pelvis is put before the major calyx; the pelvis is the last wide space in the kidney and continues directly as the ureter.

solution: The narrow tip of a pyramid is the renal papilla. From there urine is received by a minor calyx, which drains into a major calyx, then into the renal pelvis, and the pelvis continues as the ureter.
formula_principle: Urine leaves the renal papilla, is collected by a minor calyx, then a major calyx, then the renal pelvis, and finally passes into the ureter.
common_misconception: Students confuse minor with major calyx and place the renal pelvis before the calyces because it is the largest space.

concept_tested: Applying the stated definitions of pyramid and column to identify the tissue lying between two adjacent pyramids
stem: Take the following as the rule: the renal pyramids are the conical arrangement of the medullary structures, and the renal columns, also called the columns of Bertini, are extensions of the cortex lying between the pyramids. A student examining a longitudinal section concludes that every part of the kidney lying deeper than the outer rim must be medullary. Which observation shows this conclusion to be wrong?

options.A: The pyramids themselves are built of cortical tissue and are separated by strips of medulla
options.B: Strips of cortical tissue run inwards between adjacent pyramids as the columns of Bertini
options.C: The renal capsule sends fibrous strips inwards between adjacent pyramids
options.D: The minor calyces send outward extensions of the pelvis between adjacent pyramids

correct_answer_text: Strips of cortical tissue run inwards between adjacent pyramids as the columns of Bertini

distractor_rationale.A: This reverses the rule; the pyramids are the medullary masses and the strips between them are cortical.
distractor_rationale.C: The renal capsule is a covering membrane on the outside of the kidney and does not form the tissue strips between pyramids.
distractor_rationale.D: The calyces are urine collecting spaces that receive the papillae; they do not extend outwards as tissue between the pyramids.

solution: Cortical tissue is not restricted to the outer rim of the kidney. It extends inwards between adjacent medullary pyramids as the renal columns, so tissue lying deep in the kidney can still be cortex.
formula_principle: Renal pyramids are medullary, but the cortex is not confined to the rim: it sends the renal columns, or columns of Bertini, inwards between adjacent pyramids.
common_misconception: Students treat cortex and medulla as two simple concentric shells and forget that the cortex dips inwards between the pyramids.

concept_tested: Explaining prevention of backflow of urine when the ureteric openings carry no valves
stem: Take the following as the rule: the two ureters open into the urinary bladder by separate openings, and these openings are NOT guarded by valves. Even so, urine does not flow back into the ureters when a full bladder is compressed. What accounts for this?

options.A: The ureters pass obliquely through the wall of the bladder, so compression closes them
options.B: The two openings lie so far apart on the bladder wall that urine cannot reach them
options.C: A ring of skeletal muscle around each opening contracts as the bladder fills
options.D: The transitional epithelium of the bladder seals each opening as the bladder stretches

correct_answer_text: The ureters pass obliquely through the wall of the bladder, so compression closes them

distractor_rationale.B: The openings form the two basal corners of the trigone and are not beyond the reach of urine; their separation does not stop backflow.
distractor_rationale.C: Skeletal muscle in this region forms the external urethral sphincter at the outlet of the bladder, not rings around the ureteric openings.
distractor_rationale.D: The transitional epithelium allows the bladder wall to stretch; it is a lining tissue and does not act as a closing mechanism.

solution: Each ureter runs obliquely through the thickness of the bladder wall. When the bladder is compressed, the pressure squeezes this oblique stretch shut, so urine cannot be driven back up the ureter even though no valve guards the opening.
formula_principle: Backflow of urine from the bladder into the ureters is prevented not by valves but by the oblique passage of each ureter through the bladder wall.
common_misconception: Students assume that wherever backflow is prevented in the body there must be a valve, and invent one at the ureteric opening.

stem: The urinary bladder is a hollow muscular organ whose innermost lining helps it to stretch as it fills. Where does the bladder lie, and which epithelium forms this lining?

options.C: In the pelvic cavity, posterior to the pubic symphysis; lined by transitional epithelium

formula_principle: The urinary bladder lies in the pelvic cavity posterior to the pubic symphysis and is lined internally by transitional epithelium, which permits stretching.

subtopic: Path of the filtrate through the nephron
concept_tested: Order of the first parts of the nephron traversed by the filtrate
stem: Fluid filtered out of the glomerulus first collects in a space within Bowman's capsule and then travels along the renal tubule. Which sequence gives the order in which it passes through the following parts?

options.A: Capsular space --> proximal convoluted tubule --> neck --> descending limb --> ascending limb
options.B: Neck --> capsular space --> proximal convoluted tubule --> ascending limb --> descending limb
options.C: Capsular space --> neck --> proximal convoluted tubule --> descending limb --> ascending limb
options.D: Capsular space --> neck --> descending limb --> proximal convoluted tubule --> ascending limb

correct_answer_text: Capsular space --> neck --> proximal convoluted tubule --> descending limb --> ascending limb

distractor_rationale.A: The neck is the short ciliated connection between the capsule and the proximal convoluted tubule, so it cannot follow that tubule.
distractor_rationale.B: Filtration delivers fluid into the capsular space first, and the loop of Henle is descended before it is ascended.
distractor_rationale.D: This places the loop of Henle before the proximal convoluted tubule, whereas the loop follows that tubule.

formula_principle: The filtrate passes from the capsular space through the neck into the proximal convoluted tubule and then into the descending and ascending limbs of the loop of Henle in that order.
common_misconception: Students omit the neck altogether or insert it after the proximal convoluted tubule, and reverse the two limbs of the loop.

subtopic: Path of blood through the kidney
concept_tested: Order of the renal vessels traversed by blood entering the kidney
stem: Blood entering the kidney passes through a definite series of vessels before it is carried away. Which sequence gives the order in which it passes through the following?

options.A: Renal artery --> efferent arteriole --> glomerulus --> afferent arteriole --> peritubular capillary network --> renal venule
options.B: Renal artery --> afferent arteriole --> glomerulus --> peritubular capillary network --> efferent arteriole --> renal venule
options.C: Renal artery --> afferent arteriole --> glomerulus --> efferent arteriole --> peritubular capillary network --> renal venule
options.D: Renal artery --> afferent arteriole --> efferent arteriole --> glomerulus --> peritubular capillary network --> renal venule

correct_answer_text: Renal artery --> afferent arteriole --> glomerulus --> efferent arteriole --> peritubular capillary network --> renal venule

distractor_rationale.A: The two arterioles are interchanged; the afferent arteriole is the one that brings blood towards the glomerulus.

distractor_rationale.D: The glomerulus is placed after the efferent arteriole, although the efferent arteriole drains the glomerulus.

formula_principle: Renal blood flows through the renal artery, the afferent arteriole, the glomerulus, the efferent arteriole, the peritubular capillary network and then the renal venule.

stem: A small dissolved molecule enters the kidney in the blood, is filtered out at the glomerulus and then travels along the nephron. Which sequence gives the order in which it meets the following structures?

options.B: Renal artery --> efferent arteriole --> glomerulus --> capsular space --> neck --> proximal convoluted tubule
options.C: Renal artery --> afferent arteriole --> glomerulus --> capsular space --> neck --> proximal convoluted tubule
options.D: Renal artery --> afferent arteriole --> glomerulus --> neck --> capsular space --> proximal convoluted tubule

options.C: Afferent arteriole --> vasa recta --> glomerulus --> efferent arteriole --> renal venule

options.B: It is a juxtamedullary nephron, the capillaries around its loop are the glomerular capillaries, and the densely packed tubule cells form the JG cells

options.D: It is a cortical nephron, the capillaries around its loop are the glomerular capillaries, and the densely packed tubule cells form the JG cells

concept_tested: Computing effective filtration pressure from the glomerular, osmotic and capsular pressures
stem: In the glomerulus the hydrostatic pressure is about 55 mm Hg, the osmotic pressure of the blood is about 30 mm Hg and the hydrostatic pressure of the filtrate in the capsular space is about 15 mm Hg. Effective filtration pressure equals the hydrostatic pressure in the glomerulus minus the sum of the osmotic pressure of the blood and the filtrate hydrostatic pressure. What is the effective filtration pressure?

distractor_rationale.A: This is obtained by subtracting only the osmotic pressure of the blood and ignoring the hydrostatic pressure of the filtrate in the capsular space.
distractor_rationale.C: This is obtained by subtracting only the filtrate hydrostatic pressure and ignoring the osmotic pressure of the blood.
distractor_rationale.D: This is the sum of all three pressures; the two opposing pressures must be subtracted from the glomerular hydrostatic pressure, not added to it.

solution: The two opposing pressures total 30 + 15 = 45 mm Hg. Subtracting this from the glomerular hydrostatic pressure of 55 mm Hg gives an effective filtration pressure of 10 mm Hg.
formula_principle: Effective filtration pressure = hydrostatic pressure in glomerulus - (osmotic pressure of blood + filtrate hydrostatic pressure).
common_misconception: Students subtract only one of the two opposing pressures, or add all three values, because they do not fix which pressures drive filtration and which oppose it.

concept_tested: Recovering an unknown opposing pressure from a stated effective filtration pressure
stem: For a nephron the effective filtration pressure is 10 mm Hg and the hydrostatic pressure in the glomerulus is 55 mm Hg. The osmotic pressure of the blood is 30 mm Hg. Effective filtration pressure equals the hydrostatic pressure in the glomerulus minus the sum of the osmotic pressure of the blood and the hydrostatic pressure of the filtrate. What is the hydrostatic pressure of the filtrate in the capsular space?

distractor_rationale.A: This is the total of both opposing pressures; the osmotic pressure of the blood still has to be removed from it to leave the filtrate hydrostatic pressure.
distractor_rationale.B: This comes from subtracting the effective filtration pressure from the osmotic pressure of the blood, which reverses the roles of the two quantities.
distractor_rationale.C: This treats the effective filtration pressure as the difference between the osmotic pressure of blood and the filtrate pressure, which is not the stated relationship.

solution: The two opposing pressures together must be 55 - 10 = 45 mm Hg. Since the osmotic pressure of the blood is 30 mm Hg, the hydrostatic pressure of the filtrate is 45 - 30 = 15 mm Hg.
formula_principle: Effective filtration pressure = hydrostatic pressure in glomerulus - (osmotic pressure of blood + filtrate hydrostatic pressure), rearranged for the filtrate pressure.
common_misconception: Students stop at the combined opposing pressure and quote it as the answer instead of separating the osmotic component from the capsular component.

concept_tested: Converting the printed filtration rate per minute into the volume of filtrate formed in a day
stem: Glomerular filtration proceeds at a rate of 125 ml per minute. Taking a day as 24 hours of 60 minutes each, what volume of glomerular filtrate is formed in one day?

distractor_rationale.A: This is a tenfold underestimate arising from a slipped decimal point while converting 180000 ml into litres.
distractor_rationale.B: This is the volume formed in 10 hours only and treats part of the day rather than the whole 24 hours.
distractor_rationale.C: This is a tenfold overestimate arising from converting millilitres to litres by dividing by 100 instead of 1000.

formula_principle: Volume per day = filtration rate per minute x 60 minutes x 24 hours, then millilitres converted to litres by dividing by 1000.

concept_tested: Applying the reabsorbed fraction of the glomerular filtrate to the filtration rate
stem: Glomerular filtrate is formed at 125 ml per minute, and about 99 per cent of the glomerular filtrate is reabsorbed in the proximal and distal convoluted tubules. What volume of filtrate is reabsorbed in one minute?

subtopic: High threshold and low threshold substances
concept_tested: Separating actively reabsorbed high threshold substances from passively reabsorbed low threshold substances
stem: In selective reabsorption, high threshold substances are absorbed actively and low threshold substances are absorbed passively. Which pairing of a substance with the manner of its reabsorption is correct?

options.A: Glucose, absorbed passively as a low threshold substance
options.B: Vitamin C, absorbed passively as a low threshold substance
options.C: Sulphates, absorbed passively as a low threshold substance
options.D: Water, absorbed actively as a high threshold substance

correct_answer_text: Sulphates, absorbed passively as a low threshold substance

distractor_rationale.A: Glucose is listed among the high threshold substances of considerable importance that are absorbed actively, not passively.
distractor_rationale.B: Vitamin C appears in the list of high threshold substances taken back actively along with glucose, amino acids and the major ions.
distractor_rationale.D: Water heads the list of low threshold substances that are absorbed passively, so its mode of absorption is misassigned here.

solution: Sulphates belong to the low threshold group, which also includes water and nitrates, and this whole group is taken back passively rather than by active transport.
formula_principle: High threshold substances such as glucose, amino acids, Vit. C, Ca++, K+, Na+ and Cl- are reabsorbed actively; low threshold substances such as water, sulphates and nitrates are reabsorbed passively.
common_misconception: Students assume every substance returned to the blood must be actively transported because reabsorption is described as selective.

concept_tested: Deducing which blood component is excluded by the permeability of the glomerular capillary wall
stem: Glomerular capillary walls are extremely thin and permeable to all major blood components except blood cells and macromolecules such as protein. Which of the following is therefore absent from the glomerular filtrate?

distractor_rationale.B: Glucose is a small solute that passes freely into the capsular space and is named among the contents of the glomerular filtrate.

concept_tested: Recognising that one ion can be reabsorbed in one region and secreted in another
stem: In selective reabsorption K+ is listed among the high threshold substances that are taken back actively from the tubular fluid into the blood. Tubular secretion, by contrast, is the movement of substances from the blood into the tubular fluid. In which region is K+ moved from the blood into the tubular fluid?

options.A: Distal convoluted tubule and collecting tubule
options.B: Proximal convoluted tubule and the neck region
options.C: Descending limb and ascending limb of Henle's loop
options.D: Bowman's capsule and the capsular space

correct_answer_text: Distal convoluted tubule and collecting tubule

distractor_rationale.B: The PCT is the main site of selective reabsorption, where K+ moves in the opposite direction, from the tubular fluid into the blood.
distractor_rationale.C: The limbs of the loop are described in terms of water and NaCl movement for the counter current mechanism, not active movement of K+ into the tubular fluid.
distractor_rationale.D: Bowman's capsule receives the glomerular filtrate, so substances arrive there by filtration rather than by active secretion.

solution: K+ together with H+ and wastes such as creatinine is actively secreted from the blood into the tubular fluid in the distal convoluted tubule and the collecting tubule, even though the same ion is reabsorbed earlier in the proximal convoluted tubule.
formula_principle: The same ion can appear in two different steps of urine formation; K+ is actively reabsorbed in the PCT and is also among the ions actively secreted in the DCT and collecting tubule.
common_misconception: Students assume that a substance appearing in the reabsorption list cannot also appear in the secretion list, and rule out K+ as a secreted ion.

concept_tested: Naming the densely packed region of the DCT wall that contacts the afferent arteriole
stem: In each nephron the beginning part of the distal convoluted tubule makes contact with the afferent arteriole of the same nephron. In this region the cells of the wall of the distal convoluted tubule are packed more densely than elsewhere. What is this region called?

distractor_rationale.A: JG cells are the modified smooth muscle cells of the wall of the afferent arteriole with granular sarcoplasm, not cells of the distal convoluted tubule.
distractor_rationale.B: Podocytes are the special squamous cells of the visceral wall of Bowman's capsule bearing pedicels, and lie nowhere near the distal convoluted tubule.
distractor_rationale.C: Peritubular capillaries are the network of blood vessels surrounding the tubule and are not a densely packed region of the tubular wall.

concept_tested: Ordering the regions of the renal tubule in the order the tubular fluid passes them
stem: Arrange the following regions of the renal tubule in the order in which the tubular fluid passes through them: collecting tubule, distal convoluted tubule, Henle's loop, proximal convoluted tubule.

options.A: Proximal convoluted tubule --> distal convoluted tubule --> Henle's loop --> collecting tubule
options.B: Henle's loop --> proximal convoluted tubule --> distal convoluted tubule --> collecting tubule
options.C: Proximal convoluted tubule --> Henle's loop --> collecting tubule --> distal convoluted tubule
options.D: Proximal convoluted tubule --> Henle's loop --> distal convoluted tubule --> collecting tubule

correct_answer_text: Proximal convoluted tubule --> Henle's loop --> distal convoluted tubule --> collecting tubule

distractor_rationale.A: This places the two convoluted tubules together, whereas Henle's loop lies between them and connects the proximal to the distal tubule.
distractor_rationale.B: This puts Henle's loop first, but the filtrate leaves the neck and enters the proximal convoluted tubule before reaching the loop.
distractor_rationale.C: This reverses the last two regions; the collecting tubule is a short straight continuation of the distal convoluted tubule and therefore follows it.

solution: The tubular fluid leaves Bowman's capsule and the neck, passes through the proximal convoluted tubule, then the U shaped Henle's loop, then the distal convoluted tubule, and finally the collecting tubule which opens into the collecting duct.
formula_principle: The renal tubule runs in a fixed order: Bowman's capsule, neck, PCT, Henle's loop, DCT, collecting tubule and then the collecting duct.
common_misconception: Students remember the two convoluted tubules as adjacent structures and insert Henle's loop after both of them.

subtopic: Structure and function of the PCT
concept_tested: Predicting the process impaired when the brush border of the PCT is lost
stem: The cells lining the proximal convoluted tubule are cuboidal and bear a brush border of microvilli, and the convolutions slow the passage of the filtrate. In a nephron in which the brush border of the proximal convoluted tubule is absent while every other structure is normal, which process is directly reduced?

options.A: Selective reabsorption of useful molecules from the tubular fluid
options.B: Glomerular filtration of plasma into the capsular space
options.C: Tubular secretion of K+ and H+ into the tubular fluid
options.D: Counter current multiplication in Henle's loop

correct_answer_text: Selective reabsorption of useful molecules from the tubular fluid

distractor_rationale.B: Filtration depends on the glomerular capillary wall and the balance of pressures at the Malpighian body, neither of which involves the brush border of the PCT.
distractor_rationale.C: Secretion of these ions occurs by active transport in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting tubule, regions unaffected by the change described.
distractor_rationale.D: The medullary gradient is built by the two limbs of Henle's loop carrying fluid in opposite directions, and does not depend on the surface of the PCT cells.

solution: The PCT is the place of selective reabsorption, and its microvillous brush border together with its convolutions is what allows maximum reabsorption of useful molecules, so losing the brush border reduces reabsorption specifically.
formula_principle: The brush border of microvilli on PCT cells provides the surface area that makes the PCT the place of selective reabsorption; structure determines the function localised there.
common_misconception: Students associate any damage to a nephron with a fall in filtration, without asking which region carries out which step.
difficulty_basis: One comparison, short interpretation or routine calculation linking up to two prescribed facts

concept_tested: Naming the capillary set that operates the counter current exchange system
stem: The osmotic gradient established in the renal medulla is maintained by a set of loop shaped capillaries that operate a counter current exchange system. Name these capillaries.

distractor_rationale.A: The peritubular capillary network surrounds the convoluted tubules for reabsorption but is not the loop shaped set described as the counter current exchanger.
distractor_rationale.B: The glomerular capillaries form the bunch where filtration occurs, and they lie in the Malpighian body rather than around Henle's loop in the medulla.
distractor_rationale.D: The afferent arteriole is a single vessel bringing blood to the glomerulus and is not a capillary network operating an exchange system.

solution: The vasa recta are the capillaries surrounding Henle's loop of juxtamedullary nephrons, and they maintain the medullary osmotic gradient by operating the counter current exchange system.
formula_principle: The limbs of Henle's loop act as the counter current multiplier and the vasa recta act as the counter current exchanger that maintains the medullary osmotic gradient.
common_misconception: Students confuse the multiplier with the exchanger and attribute the exchange system to Henle's loop or to the ordinary peritubular capillaries.

concept_tested: Distinguishing the descending and ascending limbs by wall thickness, water permeability and epithelium
stem: Which pairing of a limb of Henle's loop with its wall thickness, water permeability and lining epithelium is correct?

options.A: Descending limb, thick walled, impermeable to water, simple cuboidal epithelium
options.B: Ascending limb, thin walled, permeable to water, simple squamous epithelium
options.C: Ascending limb, thick walled, permeable to water, simple cuboidal epithelium
options.D: Descending limb, thin walled, permeable to water, simple squamous epithelium

correct_answer_text: Descending limb, thin walled, permeable to water, simple squamous epithelium

distractor_rationale.A: These are the features of the ascending limb; the descending limb is the thin walled limb through which water leaves by osmosis.
distractor_rationale.B: The ascending limb is thick walled and impermeable to water, which is why NaCl rather than water leaves it.
distractor_rationale.C: The wall thickness and epithelium are right for the ascending limb but its impermeability to water is the property that makes the counter current mechanism work.

solution: The descending limb of Henle's loop is the thin walled limb of simple squamous epithelium that is permeable to water, so water moves out of it by osmosis into the tissue fluid.
formula_principle: The descending limb is thin walled, permeable to water and lined by simple squamous epithelium; the ascending limb is thick walled, impermeable to water and lined by simple cuboidal epithelium.
common_misconception: Students remember only that the two limbs differ and attach water permeability to the ascending limb, where NaCl and not water is what leaves.

concept_tested: Comparing the osmolarity of the deep inner medulla with that of the cortex
stem: In the kidney the osmolarity of the cortex is 300 mOsmol L-1 and that of the deep inner medulla is 1200 mOsmol L-1. The osmolarity of the deep inner medulla is how many times that of the cortex?

distractor_rationale.A: This comes from taking the difference of 900 mOsmol L-1 and dividing it by 300, which gives the increase rather than the ratio.
distractor_rationale.C: This corresponds to the outer medullary value of 600 mOsmol L-1, not to the deep inner medullary value given in the stem.
distractor_rationale.D: This would need a deep inner medullary value of 1800 mOsmol L-1, which is above the highest osmolarity reached in the medulla.

concept_tested: Identifying the tubular segment that urea cannot cross
stem: During urea recycling, urea diffuses out of the urine into the tissue fluid of the medulla and later re-enters the tubule. One segment of the renal tubule is impermeable to urea and so keeps it trapped in the medullary tissue fluid. Which segment is this?

distractor_rationale.A: The proximal convoluted tubule is described as the site of bulk reabsorption of the filtrate and is not named as the barrier that traps urea in the medulla.

distractor_rationale.D: This combination includes false statement(s) III.

Statement IV is correct because 'Property in which several codons specify one amino acid' corresponds to Degeneracy. Therefore, the valid combination is I and IV only.

concept_tested: Deliberate alteration of genetic material
stem:
During error analysis, four proposed associations are reviewed.
I. Deliberate alteration of genetic material corresponds to Genetic engineering.
II. Organism carrying and expressing an introduced gene corresponds to Bioprocess engineering.
III. Maintenance of sterile conditions for industrial microbial growth corresponds to Bioprocess engineering.
IV. Transgenic plant known for insect resistance corresponds to Bt cotton.
Which set contains all and only the valid conclusions?

distractor_rationale.A: This combination includes false statement(s) II and omits true statement(s) I, III.
distractor_rationale.C: This combination omits true statement(s) I, IV.
distractor_rationale.D: This combination omits true statement(s) III, IV.

solution: Statement I is correct because 'Deliberate alteration of genetic material' corresponds to Genetic engineering. Statement II is incorrect: 'Organism carrying and expressing an introduced gene' corresponds to Transgenic organism, not Bioprocess engineering. Statement III is correct because 'Maintenance of sterile conditions for industrial microbial growth' corresponds to Bioprocess engineering. Statement IV is correct because 'Transgenic plant known for insect resistance' corresponds to Bt cotton. Therefore, the valid combination is I, III and IV only.
